newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bonds seek fuel to test 112-24.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bonds seek fuel to test 112-24.

text.p: U.S. T-bond futures were at a technical cross-roads, and any soft U.S. employment data on Thursday would recharge the market for a test of 112-24, technical analysts said.
T-bonds were held by strong layers of support and strengthened by Wednesday's rebound above 102-00, but lacked the stamina to cross the June 20 peak.
"The payrolls data is going to be the deciding factor," said a technical analyst at Merrill Lynch in London.
"It could go either way. The way it is trading at the moment there is no strong impetus but a slight lenience to the upside," he added.
By 1014 GMT, September T-bonds were quoted 4/32 higher on the day at 112-06 in automated trade. At the short end, December Eurodollars were down 0.005 at 93.960.
A Reuters poll of economists forecast June payrolls to increase by 222,000, compared with 138,000 in May. The rate of unemployment was expected steady at 4.8 percent. The data are due at 1230 GMT.
Mike Macdonald, technical analyst at 4CAST in London, said any near-term gains would be capped at 112-24.
"The recent fall from 112-24 is possibly going to be corrected further," he said. "Runs up to there could prove difficult initially."
But if 112-24 broke, September T-bonds would march towards the February 18 low of 112-27 and an up trend channel coming in at 113-18 and further up towards 114-00.
The Merrill Lynch analyst said the market was trapped in a well-worn range between 110-30 to 112-27, which provided initial support at 112-15.
"The risk is that if the market does fail from here it can head back down towards 111-20," he added. That level was intraday congestion.
Further down, Macdonald saw trendline support at 110-31, providing a strong cushion.
Donna Liu, technical analyst at DKB International in London, said the market was constrained on the upside at 112-25 and needed to get through that level to boost its upside chances.
"Otherwise the market will try the downside," she said.
